reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: IgM anti HBc marks acute hepatitis B; HBsAg alone does not stage it
Portal hypertension triad: ascites, varices, splenomegaly
Mallory Denk bodies suggest alcohol hepatitis but are not specific
Acute liver failure equals coagulopathy plus encephalopathy without prior cirrhosis
reference.pathophysiology: Immune attack on infected hepatocytes (more than direct viral killing in hepatitis B) produces lobular necrosis that heals by stellate cell fibrosis when injury persists. Bridging fibrosis and nodules distort flow, raising portal pressure while portosystemic shunting and vasodilation drive ascites, varices and encephalopathy.
additionalDifferentials: Acute versus chronic viral hepatitis serology
Alcohol versus metabolic steatohepatitis histology overlap
Acute liver failure versus decompensated cirrhosis
additionalInvestigations: Viral serology panel with HCV RNA and HBV DNA quantification
Transient elastography and ultrasound for fibrosis and portal signs
INR, albumin, bilirubin and platelets for synthetic severity scoring
